seeds: Where exactly in the chain does NADH donate its electrons — which complex?
What happens to the electrons after FADH2 donates them at Complex II?
Why does FADH2 produce less ATP than NADH when both donate electrons?
What molecule accepts the electrons from Complexes I and II before they reach Complex III?
parsed.rendering_md:
Your question is covered by an existing node: **NADH and FADH2 as electron donors** (node n_b4m7gx1pz6wqdce8nv3sk0rty2).

NADH carries high-energy electrons to **Complex I** (NADH dehydrogenase) at the start of the electron transport chain. FADH2 carries its electrons to **Complex II** (succinate dehydrogenase). From both entry points the electrons are passed along to ubiquinone (coenzyme Q), then to Complex III, then via cytochrome c to Complex IV, and finally to oxygen. Each electron handoff at Complexes I, III, and IV is coupled to pumping protons across the inner membrane, building the gradient that drives ATP synthesis. Because FADH2 enters at Complex II — which does not pump protons — it drives the production of fewer ATP molecules than NADH.
